recent_posts.title: #214 – Robby McCullough on Beaver Builder, AI Hype, and Evolving WordPress Workflows
recent_posts.summary: Robby McCullough, co-founder of Beaver Builder, joins the WP Tavern podcast to discuss the 12-year journey of the WordPress page builder, the impact of AI on web development workflows, and why Beaver Builder deliberately avoided early AI hype. Robby shares that the team is now actively experimenting with agentic AI features, including drag-to-import vibe-coded pages and an in-editor chat agent. The conversation explores whether page builders still have a role in an AI-first world, with both hosts concluding that visual editing tools will remain valuable for maintenance and fine-tuning even as AI handles initial site creation. They also reflect on the loss of craftsmanship, the pace of technological change, the decline of WordPress community events, and the human cost of increasingly AI-mediated work.

recent_posts.title: #213 – Malcolm Peralty on Managed WordPress Hosting and AI Innovation at Pressable
recent_posts.summary: Malcolm Peralty, technical account manager at Pressable, discusses the realities of managed WordPress hosting, from performance challenges with plugin-heavy sites and WooCommerce to infrastructure innovations like database replication and virtual clusters. He explains how Pressable's upcoming MCP (AI-powered control panel) will let agencies manage WordPress sites using natural language — spinning up sandboxes, updating plugins across thousands of sites, and eventually integrating with WordPress Core's AI features. The conversation also covers the hidden costs AI bots impose on hosting infrastructure, the importance of audit logs and backups as AI automation grows, and the challenge of balancing human relationships with increasing automation.

recent_posts.title: #212 – Anne Bovelett on How Web Accessibility Boosts Traffic, SEO, and Revenue
recent_posts.summary: Accessibility strategist Anne Bovelett makes the economic case for web accessibility on WordPress sites, citing Semrush research across 10,000 websites showing compliant sites achieve 23% more organic traffic, 27% more keyword rankings, and a 90% boost in authority scores. She references the Click Away Pound Report, which found UK e-commerce sites lost £17 billion in 2019 by being inaccessible, and notes that 75% of disabled customers will pay more to shop on an accessible site. Bovelett argues that poor semantic HTML, overuse of div/span elements, and JavaScript-heavy frameworks harm both screen readers and search engine crawlers equally. She also highlights reduced support costs as a benefit, citing a Dutch tax office that saw 30% fewer support requests after an accessibility redesign.

recent_posts.title: #211 – Elliott Richmond on WordPress Content Creation, Education, and Pizza Plugins
recent_posts.summary: Elliott Richmond, a 20+ year WordPress developer and YouTube content creator, discusses his journey from early b2/WordPress days to running a pizza delivery business powered by WooCommerce and custom plugins. He shares how he built a delivery slot system with geolocation radius restrictions, now being packaged as a freemium plugin. Elliott also reveals a new arrangement with Automattic to create educational video content about wordpress.com features throughout 2026, with early access to upcoming features. He covers his content creation process including loose scripting, using AI to polish brain dumps, and a minimal tech setup (iPhone camera, DIY cat-food-box lighting, DaVinci Resolve).

recent_posts.title: #210 – Zach Stepek on the Interconnected WordPress Ecosystem, Partnerships and Trust
recent_posts.summary: Zach Stepek, a WordPress and WooCommerce veteran, discusses the three interconnected pillars of the WordPress ecosystem: agencies, product companies, and hosting infrastructure. He argues these layers form a Celtic-knot-like interdependency where each must support the others to thrive. The conversation explores how ROI-driven, transactional thinking driven by private equity and economic fear is eroding the trust-based, values-driven partnerships that made WordPress successful. Zach makes the case that relationship equity precedes revenue, that community perception compounds over time, and that short-term thinking damages brand equity. He also touches on hardware component shortages threatening hosting economics and the need for better recognition of community contributions.

recent_posts.title: #209 – Simon Pollard on Navigating the New Normal for WordPress Community and Events
recent_posts.summary: A podcast conversation between Nathan Wrigley and Simon Pollard about the state of WordPress Meetups and community events post-pandemic. Simon shares his personal journey organizing the Bristol WordPress Meetup, how COVID-19 effectively ended its momentum, and his recent return to the community. They discuss why attendance hasn't recovered to pre-2020 levels, the fragmentation of social media making outreach harder, the role AI is playing in reducing community-driven knowledge sharing, and ideas for revitalizing events by mixing in music, entertainment, and non-WordPress talks to attract broader audiences.

recent_posts.title: #208 – Behind the Scenes at the CloudFest Hackathon
recent_posts.summary: A behind-the-scenes look at the CloudFest Hackathon, a non-commercial, open source collaborative event held at Europa-Park in Germany. Hackathon lead Carole Olinger explains the organization process, project selection, and attendee matching across 110 participants from 300-400 applicants. Multiple project contributors share what they built in three days, including a CMS Cloud Manager, federated events via ActivityPub, WP-CLI with MCP/AI integration, an HTML-to-CMS migration tool, AI-powered accessibility tools, accessible infographics plugin, a peer-to-peer federated RAG framework, and a WordPress staging environment manager. The event emphasizes cross-CMS collaboration (WordPress, TYPO3, Joomla, Drupal) and contributing back to FOSS rather than building proprietary products.

recent_posts.title: #207 – Rob Ruiz on WP Rig and the Future of Theme Development
recent_posts.summary: Rob Ruiz, current maintainer of WP Rig, discusses the free and open source WordPress theme development toolkit in a podcast interview. WP Rig provides a minimal starter theme with modern tooling including Composer, Node.js, PostCSS/Lightning CSS, esbuild, and ESLint to enforce WordPress coding standards. The conversation covers who WP Rig is for (from beginners to agency developers), how it compares to page builders, its support for classic, hybrid, and block-based theme paradigms including FSE and theme-level block authoring, and the recently released version 3 which significantly overhauled the build toolchain. Rob emphasizes WP Rig's educational value and its role in encouraging more WordPress contributors.

recent_posts.title: #206 – Jonathan Desrosiers on WordPress Sustainability, Community Engagement, and Release Strategies
recent_posts.summary: Jonathan Desrosiers, a WordPress Core committer and principal software engineer at Bluehost, discusses plans to synchronize WordPress major releases with flagship WordCamp events in 2026. The conversation covers the logistical challenges of aligning release schedules with international events (including religious holidays and regional factors), adoption data showing WordPress 6.9 reached 50% of all sites in just 10 days, and strategies to make releases more visible and exciting for users. The discussion also addresses the post-COVID decline in WordPress Meetup attendance, the geographic disparity between thriving APAC communities and struggling US communities, and initiatives like contributor mentorship programs and educational outreach to attract younger contributors. Both speakers reflect on how AI is empowering a new generation of builders and potentially rekindling interest in open-source platforms over walled gardens.

recent_posts.title: #205 – Matt Cromwell on Redefining WordPress Product Growth in a Crowded Ecosystem
recent_posts.summary: Matt Cromwell, co-founder of GiveWP and former StellarWP leader, discusses the current state of the WordPress product ecosystem and his new agency Roots & Fruit. He argues that the era of 'build it and they will come' is over — the plugin directory has doubled in size, competition from SaaS has intensified, and post-COVID budgets tightened. The path forward requires WordPress product makers to think like product businesses, not code businesses: prioritizing customer journey, branding, and marketing over technical execution. Matt now serves as a fractional Chief Growth Officer for small product teams and a coach for solo founders, helping them focus on high-impact growth activities instead of scattered tactics.
